l1_connect_account.title: Connect accounts that are outside the platform
l1_connect_account.why: The account exists in billing, the organization hierarchy or SSO but is not connected, so nothing in it is inventoried or checked.
steps: Ask the spend owner for read-only auditor access (metadata only, least privilege).
Prefer an organization-level connector over per-account connections.
Confirm the account appears in the inventory within 7 days.
l1_connect_account.success: Account is connected and inventoried within 7 days.
l1_connect_account.question: Which of these accounts matter most to your business this quarter, and what has made them hard to connect so far?
l1_connect_account.we_commit: send you the list of unconnected accounts with last spend and suggested owners within two working days

l1_auto_onboarding.title: Enable automatic onboarding of new accounts
l1_auto_onboarding.why: Accounts created in the last 30 days are not connected. Manual onboarding will leak again.
steps: Switch the connector to organization or management-group scope.
Add new-account detection to the monthly account review.
Alert the TAM when billing shows a new account.
l1_auto_onboarding.success: New accounts connect without a ticket.
l1_auto_onboarding.question: How do new accounts get created today, and who hears about it?
l1_auto_onboarding.we_commit: write up how new accounts are detected today and what would have to change

l2_enable_inventory.title: Close an inventory blind spot
l2_enable_inventory.why: The account is connected, but this resource type is not inventoried, so downstream checks cannot see it.
steps: Check the connector role and scopes for this resource type.
Add the missing permissions and trigger a rescan.
Verify the type appears in the inventory (zero resources is fine, unreadable is not).
l2_enable_inventory.success: Resource type is marked inventoried on every connected account.
l2_enable_inventory.question: What would you want to be certain we can see in these accounts?
l2_enable_inventory.we_commit: list the permissions each connector is missing, per account, within two working days

l3_enable_module.title: Switch on a relevant module
l3_enable_module.why: Assets that this module applies to are known, but the module is not active for them.
steps: Start with the highest-exposure assets (internet-facing, sensitive data).
Run a 30-minute enablement session with the owning team.
Record the activation date so adoption can be tracked.
l3_enable_module.success: Module active on all relevant accounts.
l3_enable_module.question: What would make switching this on worth it for the team that owns these accounts?
l3_enable_module.we_commit: run a 30-minute session for the owning team before the due date

l3_new_release_adoption.title: Adopt a capability released after the baseline
l3_new_release_adoption.why: A module released after the frozen baseline is relevant to this estate and not yet active. The bar rose; this is new headroom, not a regression.
steps: Send a short brief: what shipped, why it matters for this estate.
Offer a demo to the owning team within 30 days.
Track activation within 60 days of release.
l3_new_release_adoption.success: Capability active within 60 days of release.
l3_new_release_adoption.question: Where in your estate would you most want this capability, and what would it have to prove to earn its place?
l3_new_release_adoption.we_commit: send a one-page brief on what shipped and why it matters here, and offer a demo within 30 days

l4_assign_owners.title: Give unowned findings an owner and a decision
l4_assign_owners.why: Findings past the triage window have no owner, so nobody is accountable for a decision.
steps: Map owners from tags, project or service ownership, and code owners.
Route what cannot be mapped to the account owner for assignment.
Record the decision (fix, accepted risk, exception, false positive) at the same time.
Track the unowned share weekly.
l4_assign_owners.success: Every triaged finding has an owner and a decision.
l4_assign_owners.question: When a finding has no obvious owner, who ends up deciding, and how?
l4_assign_owners.we_commit: send the findings without an owner, with owners suggested from tags and code ownership, within two working days

l4_record_decisions.title: Record a decision on owned findings
l4_record_decisions.why: The finding has an owner but no decision. Ignoring without review is the leak; accepting consciously is not.
steps: For each finding choose: fix, accepted risk (reason and expiry), exception, or false positive.
Review in the next weekly security sync.
Close the loop in the ticketing system.
l4_record_decisions.success: Every triaged finding has a decision.
l4_record_decisions.question: Which decisions are slow because people lack information, and which because of priorities?
l4_record_decisions.we_commit: prepare the list of undecided findings for your next security sync

l4_review_accepted_risks.title: Fix accepted risks with no or expired review date
l4_review_accepted_risks.why: An accepted risk without an expiry, or with an expired one, is indistinguishable from ignoring it.
steps: Add a reason and an expiry to every accepted risk.
Re-decide the ones that have expired.
Adopt a policy that accepted risks expire by default.
l4_review_accepted_risks.success: All accepted risks have a reason and a future expiry.
l4_review_accepted_risks.question: How do you decide today that a risk is acceptable, and when does that decision get looked at again?
l4_review_accepted_risks.we_commit: draft a default expiry policy for accepted risks for you to edit

l4_review_reclassifications.title: Review severity downgrades close to the SLA deadline
l4_review_reclassifications.why: Downgrades that land just before a deadline make the metric look better without reducing risk.
steps: List findings downgraded within the review window before their SLA date.
Ask the owner for the reason; revert the ones without one.
Report the count in the next review.
l4_review_reclassifications.success: No unexplained downgrades near SLA deadlines.
l4_review_reclassifications.question: How are severity changes decided, and who gets to see them?
l4_review_reclassifications.we_commit: list the downgrades that landed near a deadline, with who made them

reach_onboard_team.title: Onboard teams that own cloud assets but have no active user
reach_onboard_team.why: Findings for these teams are read by someone else, if at all.
steps: Identify the team lead and a security champion.
Create a scoped project or role for the team.
Run a first-use session on the team's own findings.
reach_onboard_team.success: Team has a weekly active user.
reach_onboard_team.question: What does that team need from security to ship faster?
reach_onboard_team.we_commit: prepare the team's own findings, so the first session is about their work and not the product

reach_enable_sso.title: Put team access behind SSO
reach_enable_sso.why: Access outside SSO escapes joiner-mover-leaver controls.
steps: Map the team to an identity-provider group.
Enforce SSO for the team's role.
Remove local accounts.
reach_enable_sso.success: All team access comes through SSO.
reach_enable_sso.question: What stands between this team and your single sign-on?
reach_enable_sso.we_commit: map the team to an identity-provider group for you to confirm

reach_scope_roles.title: Scope roles to the team's own projects
reach_scope_roles.why: Broad roles hide ownership and over-expose findings.
steps: Create team-scoped roles.
Move users to them.
Retire broad roles.
reach_scope_roles.success: Team uses a role scoped to its projects.
reach_scope_roles.question: What would a role scoped to this team's projects have to allow for them to use it?
reach_scope_roles.we_commit: draft the scoped role for you to review

reach_access_review.title: Run an access review
reach_access_review.why: No access review in the last 90 days for a team that owns cloud assets.
steps: Export the team's users and roles.
Ask the team lead to confirm or revoke.
Record the review date.
reach_access_review.success: Access reviewed in the last 90 days.
reach_access_review.question: Who should be able to see this team's findings, and who is there that should not be?
reach_access_review.we_commit: export the team's users and roles for review

ent_adoption_gap.title: Close the gap between what is licensed and what is used
ent_adoption_gap.why: A large share of a licensed unit is not in use. Unused entitlement is a renewal risk and a coverage gap.
steps: Find where the unit would add the most value (internet-facing, sensitive workloads).
Agree a deployment plan with the owner and a date.
Review utilization monthly until it passes the threshold.
ent_adoption_gap.success: Utilization at or above the target for the unit.
ent_adoption_gap.question: If you were deciding again today, how much of this would you buy?
ent_adoption_gap.we_commit: show where each unused unit would add the most, and say plainly if the answer is that you need fewer

rel_find_sponsor.title: Find or confirm an executive sponsor
rel_find_sponsor.why: Nobody at executive level is on record as caring about this program, so priorities are set without you in the room.
steps: Ask your champion who decides on security priorities and who answers for the result.
Offer that person a short, candid view of where things stand, not a product walkthrough.
Agree one recurring touchpoint, however short.
rel_find_sponsor.success: An executive sponsor is recorded and has been spoken to in the last 90 days.
rel_find_sponsor.question: Who in your leadership cares most about how this goes, and what do they want to know?
rel_find_sponsor.we_commit: send your champion a one-page candid summary they can forward

rel_reconnect.title: Reconnect with key people you have not spoken to in 90 days
rel_reconnect.why: People who matter have heard from you only when something was being sold or fixed. Trust is kept up between projects, not only during them.
steps: Send something useful that has nothing to do with renewal or expansion: an insight about their own estate.
Ask one open question and listen to the answer.
Make no ask.
rel_reconnect.success: Every key contact has been spoken to in the last 90 days.
rel_reconnect.question: What is on your mind about security that nobody has asked you about lately?
rel_reconnect.we_commit: send one useful finding about their estate with no ask attached

rel_widen.title: Reduce dependence on a single contact
rel_widen.why: Fewer than two people have heard from you recently. If that person leaves or goes quiet, so does the account.
steps: Ask your main contact who else should be in the loop and why.
Invite one more person to the next review, with a reason that is theirs.
Share notes from meetings so others can see the value without being there.
rel_widen.success: At least two people touched in the last 90 days.
rel_widen.question: Who else is affected by this and would want to see it?
rel_widen.we_commit: share the notes from the last review with the people you name

rel_introduce.title: Get introduced to teams you have no contact in
rel_introduce.why: These teams own cloud assets and have no relationship with you. Trust does not transfer from your champion to people who have never heard of you.
steps: Learn the team's situation first, with your own time, before asking for anything.
Ask your champion for an introduction and say what is in it for the team and for the champion.
Offer the team something useful at the first meeting.
rel_introduce.success: A contact exists in every team that owns cloud assets.
rel_introduce.question: Which team would benefit most from hearing about this, and what would they want from it?
rel_introduce.we_commit: prepare a short note on each team's situation before any introduction

rel_close_commitments.title: Close overdue commitments
rel_close_commitments.why: Promises made to the customer are past their date. Reliability is what people experience between what you said and what happened.
steps: Deliver the overdue items or renegotiate them openly, before the customer has to ask.
Tell people early when a date will move, and why.
Make fewer, smaller promises and keep every one.
rel_close_commitments.success: No open commitment is past its due date.
rel_close_commitments.question: Is there anything we said we would do that you are still waiting for?
rel_close_commitments.we_commit: deliver or re-date every overdue item and tell you which

rel_improve_credibility.title: Strengthen credibility with the people who matter
rel_improve_credibility.why: Credibility is believed expertise, and also whether you seem to be telling the whole story. It is built by showing, not claiming.
steps: Bring a point of view backed by their own data, and say it plainly.
Say quickly and directly when you do not know.
Avoid promises that sound like boilerplate.
rel_improve_credibility.success: The weakest component for these people has improved by two points at the next review.
rel_improve_credibility.question: What would you need to see from us to be confident in our advice?
rel_improve_credibility.we_commit: bring one view backed by their own data to the next meeting

rel_improve_reliability.title: Strengthen reliability with the people who matter
rel_improve_reliability.why: Reliability is promises kept, in the way the customer likes things done: on time, in the format and rhythm they expect.
steps: Make small specific commitments and deliver them quietly.
Send material before meetings and confirm dates beforehand.
Match their style, hours and formats.
rel_improve_reliability.success: The weakest component for these people has improved by two points at the next review.
rel_improve_reliability.question: How would you like us to work with you day to day?
rel_improve_reliability.we_commit: agree how and when they want to hear from us, and stick to it

rel_improve_intimacy.title: Open a harder conversation with the people who matter
rel_improve_intimacy.why: Intimacy here means they are willing to talk to you about the hard issues. Someone has to go first, and it is you.
steps: Go first with something a little risky: a doubt, an admitted mistake, a real question.
Give them an easy way not to answer.
Ask about what the issue means for them, not only for the platform.
rel_improve_intimacy.success: The weakest component for these people has improved by two points at the next review.
rel_improve_intimacy.question: What is the part of this that worries you most and that we have not talked about?
rel_improve_intimacy.we_commit: raise one difficult topic in the next conversation, with a way out for them

rel_improve_self_orientation.title: Lower self-orientation with the people who matter
rel_improve_self_orientation.why: Customers can tell when an advisor's attention is on their own agenda: the renewal, the number, looking clever. It is the biggest drag because it divides everything else.
steps: Start the next meeting by sharing the agenda and asking them to add to it.
Give away an idea that has no link to renewal or expansion.
Ask before proposing, and listen before answering.
rel_improve_self_orientation.success: The weakest component for these people has improved by two points at the next review.
rel_improve_self_orientation.question: What would make this a better use of your time?
rel_improve_self_orientation.we_commit: send the agenda in advance and leave room for theirs
